reason: Verified in the source and by driving the page. render-b.js builds the readout once as F.fmt.longYear(target.date) + ' · in N days' and then move() overwrites it with 'in ' + current + ' days' — the date is gone on the first press and never returns in either direction. Measured at 1440: 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days' (347px) becomes 'in 24 days' (99px). It is worse than the finding states: .b-stepRow is flex-wrap and the 347px readout wraps the row, so the first press collapses the row from 90px to 40px and throws the +1 and +7 buttons 209px to the right and 50px up — the control the owner is about to press again jumps out from under the cursor (390px: row 168px → 123px). move() also only tracks the day count, so the edited row keeps '.b-date' = 'Sat 8 Aug' and the grab button keeps aria-label '… Saturday 8 August, in 23 days' while '.b-away' reads 16: the row contradicts itself on screen and lies to a screen reader. The reversibility line is a literal in render-b.js ('the invitations moved seven days closer'), never touched by move(), so it still claims seven days after a one-day move — words for a figure, and not derived from what happened. Neither point is proven by the gates: interaction-check.mjs only asserts readout.includes(String(away)), which passes with or without the date. No constraint is touched — no colour, no weight, no family, no architecture.
sharpenedFix: Three edits, all in the real sources, not master.html. (1) fixture.js: expose one accessor beside daysTo, e.g. dateAway(n) returning the ISO date TODAY + n days, so distance and date can never disagree. (2) render-b.js move(): derive iso = F.dateAway(current) once and drive everything from it — read.textContent = F.fmt.longYear(iso) + ' · in ' + current + ' days' (‘tomorrow’ at 1, ‘today’ at 0), item.querySelector('.b-date').textContent = F.fmt.weekdayShort(iso) + ' ' + F.fmt.short(iso), and re-set the .b-grab aria-label from the same iso and count; then set the .b-undo sentence from the same numbers in figures with the real delta and direction — 'Last change: Send the invitations moved 7 days closer.' / '1 day later.' — and seed that sentence at first render from the same builder rather than hard-coding it. (3) b.css: stop the steppers moving. Make .b-stepRow a two-row grid (buttons on row 1, .b-stepRead spanning row 2) or give the readout flex-basis:100% so it always sits on its own line; the four buttons then hold one geometry at every width and every string length. .b-stepRead already carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; keep it and add it to the .b-undo figure so the counts do not jitter. Re-run interaction-check.mjs — its 'both readouts agree after a move' assertion still passes on the fuller string.
